object_description: compact stepped volume with a three-storey central foyer
design_condition: The building fills the site between neighboring structures while maintaining appropriate distances, stepping upward to respond to surrounding heights and a change in terrain.

positive.statement: The grading of the volume responds subtly to the surrounding buildings in terms of height development and to the jump in the terrain.

position.rationale: Stepped upper massing is clearly visible in elevations and the top footprint.

positive.statement: The central interior space forms a three-storey foyer that gives the school its identity and becomes the heart of the complex.

position.rationale: Central void and vertically continuous foyer are indicated by the interior opening and elevation patterns.

positive.statement: The skillful organization of the floor plans results in an interesting sectional solution.

position.rationale: Layered floor and roof profiles show the sectional organization across elevations.

positive.statement: The proposed construction and façade design promise a concise and appropriate appearance in the neighborhood.

position.rationale: The rectilinear façade envelope is directly visible on the sampled elevations.

positive.statement: The windows, ventilated façade, and choice of materials generally point to a sustainable construction method.

position.rationale: Façade openings are visible, but ventilation components and material sustainability are not identifiable.

positive.statement: The compact volume and restrained façade have a cost-advantageous effect.

position.rationale: Compact stepped envelope is clearly sampled across all views.

positive.statement: The design integrates naturally into the existing quarter and could make a new mark on the street.

position.rationale: The street-facing edge is localized on the southern façade; neighborhood context is not represented.

negative.statement: The entrance sequence is not ideal in terms of accessibility and dimensions.

position.rationale: Entrance is approximated at the southern lower edge, with accessibility dimensions not distinguishable.

negative.statement: The distribution of the course-room types across the floors is not optimally mixed.

position.rationale: Floors are visible, but course-room types and their distribution are not represented in the exterior sample.

negative.statement: The concept of learning islands only partially corresponds to the users' expectations.

position.rationale: Central interior placement is plausible, though learning islands are not distinguishable in the point cloud.

negative.statement: The access doors to the toilet vestibules hardly correspond to the status intended by the central light space.

position.rationale: Interior doors are approximated near the central light space but are not visibly identifiable.
